criteria.evidence: The proposal changes certificate scope without changing §5.2's machine domain D, reference result F_B, or execution semantics.
No instruction changes are proposed. The image-to-cell mapping agrees with §3.3's register-to-region binding.

The conditional permutation argument is sound with the retained exact-phase, full-tuple, dirty-system and inherited-control obligations. Preparation is established from operations rather than inspection of unknown quantum data.
Targets, costs and resource semantics are unchanged. The catalog check reproduces 219 recipes and envelope hash 5de4e4995350313e50217880ba1b95de39cd043283b726337d4894efb005d197.
Resolved image identities, invocation binding and protection of unrestricted obligations are appropriate. However, the added verdict rule overlaps both existing K74 classifications; see XV4-B01.
criteria.change: §12.2: replace the verdict classification with the mutually exclusive rule written in XV4-B01, including a nonempty fixed_regions requirement.

criteria.evidence: The mathematical hypotheses are sufficient. Independently reproduced: 64 cases, coverage 1/65536, 524288 fixed bits at A=16,W=8, and the stated raw-byte SHA-256. The tiny example lacks a specific oracle relation for a complete conformance vector.
criteria.change: Conformance vectors: state, 'For the tiny oracle, payload(x,db)=db[x]&1 and code=0 at a sufficient budget. The expected tuple is (x,t XOR (db[x]&1),f,db), with workspace clean.' For image 0102, x=0 flips t and x=1 preserves t; all 64 tuples must agree.

criteria.evidence: The cited ISA clauses, Dialect 0.3 draft §§19.9/25.2 and North Star §5.1/§8 rung 4 are accurately represented. The proposal preserves the complete SQLite rung and correctly distinguishes a certificate terminology repair from missing execution capability.

The proposal clearly separates conditional proof, evidence and executable applicability, and accurately limits its verification claims. The exact verdict integration needs correction, and the image-mutation vectors should specify which bindings remain unchanged.
criteria.change: Conformance vectors: state, 'Changing image bytes while retaining the old digest or preparation binding rejects reuse of the old claim; a consistently rebound image requires a fresh successful check and may receive its own qualified verdict.'

blocking.section: Recommended exact spec diff; ISA §12.2 K74 coverage and verdicts

steps.claim: K74 assigns proof to successful componentwise full-D exhaustive claims and evidence to successful exhaustive strict slices.

The proposed addition assigns proof_relative_to_image when all non-fixed components are full-range and all remaining components are fixed_regions bindings. It neither requires any fixed binding nor explicitly replaces K74's blanket strict-slice classification.

Consider a successful exhaustive comparison of a one-bit X action over t=0,1, with no regions or borrowed systems and fixed_regions absent or empty. Every non-fixed component is full-range and there are no remaining components, so the added condition holds vacuously: K74 assigns proof while the addition assigns proof_relative_to_image. For the proposed 64-case image slice, retained K74 instead assigns evidence while the addition assigns proof_relative_to_image.
steps.by: witness:full domain bundles=[{name:t,width:1,lo:0,hi:1}], borrowed=[], regions=[], expected table 0→1 and 1→0; witness:proposal's 64-case image slice; step:<1>1; step:<1>2

steps.claim: The amended text gives overlapping outcomes without a precedence rule. In particular, the claimed preservation of old full-D K74 labels is not secured.

blocking.fix: §12.2, preferred repair: replace K74's classification sentences with: 'After every §12.1 obligation succeeds, an exhaustive table/program/oracle claim receives exactly one verdict: proof if its domain equals unrestricted D component by component; otherwise proof_relative_to_image iff fixed_regions is nonempty, every image binding is valid, and every non-fixed component occurs exactly once with its full range; otherwise evidence. An absent fixed_regions field means an empty list. Successful sampled claims always receive evidence. Coverage remains the exact n/|D| against unrestricted D. A requested proof MUST be rejected unless the computed verdict is proof; a requested proof_relative_to_image MUST satisfy the qualified-verdict conditions.' Preserve mismatch rejection and K75 host-limit handling. Expected outcomes: the full-domain one-bit X claim receives proof with fraction 1; the exhaustive 0102 image claim receives proof_relative_to_image with 64 elements and fraction 1/65536; sampling remains evidence. Alternatively, retain K74's full-D sentence, add the explicit nonempty guard, and replace its strict-slice sentence with 'Successful exhaustive strict slices receive evidence unless they satisfy the proof_relative_to_image rule.' I prefer the single exclusive classifier.

suggestions: Conformance vectors: distinguish stale-binding mutations from valid new claims. State, 'Swapping 0102 to 0201 while retaining the original digest rejects. Rebinding to SHA-256 25dfd29c09617dcc9852281c030e5b3037a338a4712a42a21c907f259c6412a0 and establishing the new preparation permits a fresh conditional check; it does not reuse the old result.'

Hashes, catalog and consumers: distinguish certificate requests from checker outcomes. State, 'fixed_regions and any supplied label request change certificate bytes; the independently assigned qualified verdict is recorded in the checker report. Under the proposed in-version K repair, source/interface/closure and object hashes remain unchanged because §9.2 excludes certificate sections from object_hash; target and catalog bytes are unchanged.'
path_to_accept: Replace the overlapping K74 verdict rules with one exclusive classification that preserves full-D proof, requires nonempty image bindings for the qualified verdict, and assigns evidence to other successful slices. Explicitly reject requested unqualified proof for a qualified result. No machine, instruction, target or catalog change is needed.
summary: The conditional-proof design is sound, its cited premises and arithmetic check out, and it preserves North Star scope. One contract blocker remains: the exact added verdict rule overlaps existing K74 outcomes and also matches legacy full-domain claims vacuously.
